events.summary: The requested MLX PID authorization and termination-escalation hardening is complete without changing the orphan termination contract.
Complete and verified at unit and trace-gate scope; no live training or serving process was deliberately terminated during verification.

An approval review of e2r found four regressions: classify_mlx_cmdline required a lowercase python/python3 basename, but macOS re-execs the venv and CommandLineTools interpreters into a Python.framework path with basename 'Python' (capital P) ~1-1.5s after spawn, so every real MLX process classified NotMlx and Stop stopped SIGKILLing survivors while the orphan scan deleted real orphan markers; the two live scan tests spawned and scanned immediately, observing the pre-re-exec argv and passing by race instead of catching this; kill_mlx_process errored on an untracked pid even when it had already exited (reaper race), leaving a stale row because useMlx's catch skipped fetchStatus; and kill_mlx_process wrote status='killed' before terminate_pid, which can fail, leaving a live process shown as killed.

Measured on-device: spawning ~/.kubemetal/venv/bin/python3 and /usr/bin/python3 (CommandLineTools) with 'import time; time.sleep(3)', then `ps -o command= -p <pid>` ~1.5s later, both reported an absolute path ending in Python.framework/.../Resources/Python.app/Contents/MacOS/Python with basename 'Python', not 'python'/'python3'.

classify_mlx_cmdline now matches the interpreter basename case-insensitively and also accepts any argv[0] ending in Python.app/Contents/MacOS/Python (HIGH-1); the two live scans (marker.rs orphan test, session scan test) now poll ps for the target pid until its argv changes from the value captured right after spawn or ~1.5s elapse, so they observe the settled post-re-exec argv instead of racing it (HIGH-2); kill_mlx_process treats an untracked-and-dead pid as already stopped (Ok(true)) while still refusing an untracked-and-alive pid, extracted as untracked_pid_stop_outcome, and useMlx's killProcess now calls fetchStatus in a finally block so a stale row is refreshed on both success and failure (MED); and kill_mlx_process now reverts the optimistically written 'killed' training status to 'error' with the real termination error when terminate_pid fails, extracted as should_revert_optimistic_killed_status (LOW).

New and adjusted unit tests cover the measured framework-Python re-exec basename classification, the argv-settled live scans, the untracked-dead-pid stop outcome, and the optimistic 'killed' status revert on termination failure. The mlx_lifecycle suite was run twice (single-threaded and default-threaded) to confirm the argv-settle change is not flaky.

events.summary: All four approval-review regressions (HIGH-1, HIGH-2, MED, LOW) in the MLX kill-hardening change are fixed and covered by tests that would have caught them before the fix.

Complete and verified: framework-Python re-exec is classified as MLX, the live tests that would have caught the regression now wait for argv to settle, Stop no longer errors on an already-exited untracked pid and always refreshes status, and a failed termination no longer shows a live process as killed. No live training or serving process was deliberately terminated during verification.
